## Proof

**Claim:** The equation is **true** (interpreting $N = n$, the number of rows of $X$).

**Setup.** Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times p}$ with full column rank, so $X^{\mathsf T}X \in \mathbb{R}^{p \times p}$ is invertible. Let $x_i \in \mathbb{R}^p$ denote the $i$-th row of $X$ written as a column vector, i.e. $x_i = X^{\mathsf T} e_i$ where $e_i \in \mathbb{R}^n$ is the $i$-th standard basis vector. Equivalently, $x_i^{\mathsf T} = e_i^{\mathsf T} X$ is the $i$-th row of $X$.

**Define the hat matrix.** Let
$$H := X(X^{\mathsf T}X)^{-1}X^{\mathsf T} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}.$$

**Step 1: Identify each summand as a diagonal entry of $H$.** The $(i,i)$-entry of $H$ is
$$h_{ii} = e_i^{\mathsf T} H\, e_i = e_i^{\mathsf T} X (X^{\mathsf T}X)^{-1} X^{\mathsf T} e_i = (e_i^{\mathsf T} X)(X^{\mathsf T}X)^{-1}(X^{\mathsf T} e_i) = x_i^{\mathsf T}(X^{\mathsf T}X)^{-1} x_i.$$

Hence the sum in question is exactly the trace of $H$:
$$\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i^{\mathsf T}(X^{\mathsf T}X)^{-1} x_i = \sum_{i=1}^{n} h_{ii} = \operatorname{tr}(H).$$

**Step 2: Compute the trace using cyclicity.** By the cyclic property of the trace, $\operatorname{tr}(ABC) = \operatorname{tr}(CAB)$ for matrices of compatible dimensions. Applying this with $A = X$, $B = (X^{\mathsf T}X)^{-1}$, $C = X^{\mathsf T}$:
$$\operatorname{tr}(H) = \operatorname{tr}\!\big(X (X^{\mathsf T}X)^{-1} X^{\mathsf T}\big) = \operatorname{tr}\!\big((X^{\mathsf T}X)^{-1} X^{\mathsf T} X\big) = \operatorname{tr}\!\big((X^{\mathsf T}X)^{-1}(X^{\mathsf T}X)\big) = \operatorname{tr}(I_p) = p.$$

**Conclusion.** Combining Steps 1 and 2,
$$\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i^{\mathsf T}(X^{\mathsf T}X)^{-1} x_i = \operatorname{tr}(H) = p.$$

Therefore the equation is **true**. $\blacksquare$
